content:
Large language models have emerged as one of the most promising fields in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning technology. As the name suggests, they are machine learning models that are trained on vast swaths of text from the internet. By processing and understanding uncanny levels of textual data, these models can generate human-like text, providing nuanced responses to a wide variety of prompts. Leveraging the power of pattern recognition, large language models have shown impressive results in various tasks including, but not limited to, translation, summarization, and question-answering. 

Today, these models are used in numerous applications, ranging from commercial sectors like customer service and content creation, to more scientific areas like data analysis and trend prediction, enhancing the decision-making process and overall productivity. Despite the strides made in their performance, large language models also pose unique challenges concerning biases embedded in the data, the method to filter inaccurate information, as well as privacy-related issues. This paper aims to elucidate an in-depth understanding of these models and their applications, along with shedding light on the associated challenges.
